label: Copy-phase onset (last original token, <DEL>, first recall) at absolute steps 8-10 in long sequences
explanation: Fires in a narrow window around the delimiter: the last original token (t=L-1), the <DEL> step (t=L), and the first copy step (t=L+1, where the model outputs orig(1) after being fed orig(0)). It also needs a large absolute step index (t of about 8-10), so it is almost entirely in long sequences (L=8-9 carry about 88% of mass; it never fires for L<=4 and never at t<=4). The largest activations are at t=L+1. Magnitude and reliability there depend strongly on the first original token: when orig(0) is m, u, 1, b or j, the precision at t=L+1 is above 0.8, and when it is t, k, o, d or r, the precision is below 0.21. That token preference is graded and does not split into a clean set, so adding it to the predicate lowered F1. The unit is close to silent in the rest of the original phase and from recall_idx 3 onward in the copy phase. Position alone gives F1 of about 0.61 with mass recall of about 0.85; most false positives are window steps where the token-dependent component stays below threshold.
